paper.title: Wind farm layout optimization using a Gaussian-based wake model

target_contributions: Gaussian-wake wind-farm layout problem on six Mosetti/Grady grid cases
non_target_baselines: the paper comparison algorithms and literature layouts are evidence anchors, not target algorithms to reimplement

A.wind: 12 m/s from north with probability one

B.wind: 36 directions in 10-degree increments, all at 12 m/s and equal probability

C.wind: 36 directions by speeds 8, 12 and 17 m/s using the vector-digitized Fig. 6 joint distribution

paper_native_problem.decision_variables: two integer grid coordinates per turbine
paper_native_problem.objective: minimize fixed-count farm cost divided by expected farm power

model_contract.farm_cost: N times (2/3 plus exp(-0.00174 N squared)/3)

direct_predecessor.paper: A real coded genetic algorithm for solving integer and mixed integer optimization problems

inherited_facts.tournament_schedule: three independent permutations so every individual participates exactly three times
inherited_facts.target_paper_survival_completion: retain the best five percent as an explicitly declared OPTIMTOOL-style setting

public_source.status: no target-paper author implementation or data archive located

missing_information: author random seeds, initial populations, final layouts and histories
MI-LXPM operator parameters in the target paper
strict versus non-strict interpretation at exactly five rotor diameters
wake behavior below the paper's stated three-diameter model-validity threshold

conflicts_and_resolutions.conflict: Fig. 6 provides rounded vector bars but no numeric probability table
conflicts_and_resolutions.resolution: recover all rectangle heights at the displayed 0.001 precision and retain their 1.002 total without silent renormalization

conflicts_and_resolutions.conflict: an earlier T01 case-C asset produces only 18.3916 MW no-wake power for 39 turbines
conflicts_and_resolutions.resolution: do not inherit it; the new Fig. 6 extraction gives 36.506188 MW and closes within 0.01% of Table 4

conflicts_and_resolutions.conflict: target paper omits MI-LXPM operator values
conflicts_and_resolutions.resolution: use its cited direct predecessor's recommended integer-operator values

conflicts_and_resolutions.conflict: target paper says ranked best individuals survive, while the cited MI-LXPM predecessor specifies complete generational replacement
conflicts_and_resolutions.resolution: follow the target paper and retain the best five percent as a declared OPTIMTOOL-style missing setting

conflicts_and_resolutions.conflict: the five-diameter inequality and below-three-diameter wake behavior are not operationally explicit
conflicts_and_resolutions.resolution: accept distance greater than or equal to five diameters and apply Gaussian deficit only from three diameters

hpc_contract.precomputation: 36-direction squared Gaussian deficit table for every ordered grid-cell pair
hpc_contract.outer_parallel_axis: six cases by five independent paper repeats
hpc_contract.thread_lifecycle: one persistent worker team per optimization
hpc_contract.allocation_policy: preallocate and swap population, offspring and mating buffers
hpc_contract.randomness: counter-keyed events independent of worker schedule
hpc_contract.reduction: fixed direction, state and turbine order
hpc_contract.formal_resource_policy: twenty concurrent one-worker paper runs consume all twenty Waffle CPU cores without nested oversubscription

claim_boundary: academic declared reproduction of the six paper problems, equations and predecessor-completed MI-LXPM; not author-source, author-random-state or exact-layout replay
